elements.inner_text:
Problem Listen
        RL agents are sample-inefficient; injected knowledge policies stay rigid and can't be recombined or replaced across tasks.
        Humansreuse & recombine freelyvsRL agentsfixed order → retrain to edit
      
      
        Motivation Listen
        
          Treat external policies as a modular, reorderable set.
          Prior fusion (KoGuN, A2T) fixes policy order, forcing retraining.
        
        sample-efficientgeneralizablecompositionalincremental
      
      
        Contribution Listen
        
          KGRL — fuse an inner policy with many knowledge policies.
          KIAN — attention rearranges, adds, or replaces policies.
          Entropy imbalance — identified, proven, and fixed.
        
      
    

    
    
      
        Method Listen
        
          KIAN = an inner actor (the agent’s own policy) + a learnable key per knowledge policy + a state-dependent query.
          The fused policy is a weighted sum; keys are unordered, so swap a policy by swapping its key — no retraining.
        
        
          π(⋅ ∣ st)=w^in πin(⋅∣st)+∑j=1nw^gj πgj(⋅∣st)\pi(\cdot\,|\,s_t)=\hat{w}_{in}\,\pi_{in}(\cdot|s_t)+\textstyle\sum_{j=1}^{n}\hat{w}_{g_j}\,\pi_{g_j}(\cdot|s_t)π(⋅∣st​)=w^in​πin​(⋅∣st​)+∑j=1n​w^gj​​πgj​​(⋅∣st​)
          Weights w^=softmax ⁣(Φ(st) ⁣⋅ ⁣k/c)\hat{w}=\mathrm{softmax}\!\big(\Phi(s_t)\!\cdot\!k / c\big)w^=softmax(Φ(st​)⋅k/c) over the inner and knowledge keys.
        
        KIAN architecture: inner actor + knowledge policies g1–g3 fused by embedding-based attention.
      
    

    
    
      
      
        Key Results Listen
        
          Zero-shot transferBest baselineKIAN
          Empty-Random 5×5 → 16×160.530.93
          Pick-and-Place, 10× goal range0.300.72
          DoorKey-8×8 → Reach (C2S)0.801.00
        
        Only method to succeed in every environment given a sub-optimal knowledge set — the advantage grows as tasks get harder.
        Sample-efficiency learning curves across MiniGrid (top two rows) and OpenAI-Robotics (bottom). KIAN (teal) reaches high reward with far fewer samples on every task.
        Best zero-shot transfer in both simple→complex and complex→simple settings, with lower variance than every baseline (BC, RL, RL+BC, KoGuN, A2T). Methods that ignore entropy imbalance (A2T) barely learn in continuous control, while KIAN keeps improving.
      
    

    
    
      
      
        Headline Numbers
        
        
          0.93
          Zero-shot reward, 5×5 → 16×16 (vs 0.53 baseline)
          
            0.72Pick-and-Place 10× (vs 0.30)
            1.00DoorKey→Reach (vs 0.80)
            10seeds · 95% CI
          
        
      
      
        Ablation Listen
        
          Removing the entropy-imbalance fix collapses KIAN onto one policy.
          Compositional & incremental: reused keys learn tasks sequentially with fewer samples.
        
        Modular knowledge keys pay off across transfer settings.
      
      
        Takeaway Listen
        Encoding each policy as an independent learnable key and fusing them by attention makes external knowledge fully modular; the entropy fix keeps exploration efficient. Knowledge policies become plug-and-play building blocks.Add, drop, or reorder knowledge policies anytime — without retraining the network.
